repaired.name: Scenario
repaired.script:
triggered := false
if (triggered == true) {
    wait until((#L_Button).button_button != "pushed")
    triggered = false
}
wait until((#L_Button).button_button == "pushed")
all(#LevelControl).levelControl_moveToLevel(100, 0)
triggered = true

diagnosis.summary: The IR requires a rising-edge wait for the button condition before executing the body. The candidate uses a periodic `if` statement which only evaluates at the start of each iteration (every 1000ms). Since the input history shows the button became 'pushed' at t=0ms and held for 100ms, the IR fires immediately at t=0ms. The candidate misses this because its guard is evaluated at t=1000ms, by which time the input has already changed or the edge has passed without triggering the action.
diagnosis.change_summary: Replaced the periodic `if` guard with a blocking rising-edge wait (`wait until` with edge logic) followed by the action. This ensures the action executes exactly when the edge occurs, matching the IR's `wait(cond, rising)` behavior, rather than waiting for the next wrapper period.
